task: Write a welcome email to new students at my yoga studio. Include the studio policies I pasted: arrive 10 minutes early, cancel bookings 4 hours before class or lose the credit, no shoes on the mats, and first-timers get one free class with code WELCOME1. Keep it warm and organized so people can scan it quickly.
rewrite:
ambition: A top studio communicator would give each rule a one-clause reason ("so you can settle in before class starts", "so your mat stays clean for everyone"). New students then read the rules as care, not red tape. They would also open with a line on what the first visit feels like, so a nervous newcomer relaxes before reaching the policies.

agency: The rawest material is your pasted policies, which have to stay exact. Your own voice also matters: your past class confirmations or a sign-up page would show how you talk to students. If those aren't to hand, write in a plain, friendly studio voice, and leave a blank only for facts only you know, such as the studio name and your sign-off.

acceleration: Use the standard welcome-email layout: a short, warm subject line, one friendly opening paragraph, and a short bolded-lead-in list for the four policies. Put the free-class code on its own line so it can't be missed, and finish with a single clear next step (book your first class). Skip headers, graphics, and long paragraphs.

accuracy: Nothing in the model can check this. The nearest outside checks are to read it on a phone and see whether each of the four policies can be found in about five seconds, and to have a staff member or a recent new student say what they would do after reading it. Also confirm that WELCOME1 actually works in your booking system before sending.

answers.plain:
**Subject: Welcome to [Studio Name] 🧘**

Hi [First Name],

We're so happy you've joined us! Whether you're stepping onto a mat for the first time or returning after a break, you're welcome here exactly as you are.

**Your first class is on us**
Use code **WELCOME1** at checkout to book your free first class.

**Before you come in**

- **Arrive 10 minutes early.** This gives you time to check in, settle in, and get comfortable before class begins.
- **Leave your shoes at the door.** Please keep shoes off the mats and in the designated area.

**Booking and cancellations**

- **Cancel at least 4 hours before class.** If you cancel later than that, the class credit will be lost. If your plans change, just let us know in time and we'll happily open your spot to someone else.

**Quick recap**

- Free first class with code WELCOME1
- Arrive 10 minutes early
- No shoes on the mats
- Cancel 4+ hours ahead to keep your credit

If you have any questions, just reply to this email. We can't wait to meet you on the mat.

Namaste,
[Your Name]
[Studio Name]
[Phone / Website]

---

I used placeholders for the studio name, your name, and contact details. I can also adjust the tone, shorten it, or add things like what to bring, class types, or the address.
answers.nudge:
# Welcome email

**Subject:** Welcome to [Studio Name]. Your first class is on us 🧘
*(Alternates: "You're in! Here's everything for your first class" / "Welcome to [Studio Name], [First Name]")*

**Preview text:** Use code WELCOME1 for a free first class, plus a quick guide to what to expect.

---

Hi [First Name],

Welcome to [Studio Name]! We're so glad you're here. Whether you've practiced for years or have never touched a mat, you belong in our space, and we'll help you feel at home.

**Your free first class**
First-timers get one class on us. Use code **WELCOME1** when you book at [booking link].

**Before you come: the essentials**

🕙 **Arrive 10 minutes early.**
This gives you time to check in, find a spot, get settled, and breathe before class starts.

👟 **Leave your shoes at the door.**
No shoes on the mats, please. It keeps the practice space clean for everyone.

📱 **Need to cancel? Do it at least 4 hours before class.**
Cancel in [booking app/link] up to 4 hours before start time and your credit is safe. After that, the credit is forfeited. This keeps spots open for others on the waitlist.

**What to expect on your first visit**
- **Check in** at the front desk and tell us it's your first time. We'll show you around.
- **What to wear:** Comfortable clothes you can move and stretch in.
- **What to bring:** Water and a small towel. [Mats are available to borrow / rent for $X.]
- **Not sure what you're doing?** That's fine. Tell your teacher you're new, and they'll offer modifications. Resting in child's pose is always welcome.

**Find us**
[Street address] · [Parking/transit note] · [Entrance tip, e.g., "We're on the second floor, past the green door"]

**Questions?**
Reply to this email or reach us at [phone/email]. We read every message.

We can't wait to meet you on the mat.

Warmly,
[Your Name]
[Studio Name]
[Website] · [Instagram handle]

---

## Notes on choices I made
- **Scannable layout:** The policies are bold, one-line rules, each with a short reason. People follow rules better when they know why.
- **Order:** The free class comes first because it's the hook. The policies follow, and the reassurance section goes last so the email ends on a friendly note.
- **Tone of the cancellation rule:** I framed it around fairness to other students rather than as a penalty.
- **Placeholders:** I left brackets wherever I'd be inventing facts: studio name, links, address, mat rental, and what to wear or bring. Please fill in or delete those lines. I assumed the code is entered at online booking, so tell me if it's redeemed some other way, such as at the front desk.

If it would help, I can also write a shorter version for SMS or a follow-up email to send after their first class, asking for feedback and offering a class pack.

- **Cancel at least 4 hours before class.** Late cancellations lose the class credit, because it's hard to offer your spot to someone else on short notice.
- **No shoes on the mats.** It keeps our practice space clean and comfortable for everyone.
- **Your first class is free.** Use code below at checkout:

  **WELCOME1**

Ready to give it a try? **[Book your first class here: link]**

We can't wait to meet you.

Warmly,
[Your Name]
[Studio Name]
